title: Findings to fixes
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for turning every noticed error, issue, design flaw or annoyance into recorded, fixed and verified work: findings with evidence and a duplicate fingerprint, kind and severity guides, an evidence checklist, disclosure rules, a regression-guard template, ten verbs from recording to a periodic pattern review, and eight real public findings as worked examples.
boundaries: Every noticed problem is recorded, and failures stay on the record: nothing is deleted or rewritten to hide a mistake.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
No verb publishes, pushes, merges or deploys anything; the owner releases public summaries and lands fixes.
Security findings follow the security review pack and stay private until their fix is in effect everywhere they were seen.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for turning every noticed error, issue, design flaw or annoyance into recorded, fixed and verified work

value.lets_workers: Record every error, issue, design flaw or annoyance anyone notices as a finding with evidence, at once, then reproduce it, fold duplicates together, fix it, have a different worker verify the fix, add a guard shown to fail without the fix, close it through a gate and, when the disclosure rules allow it, prepare a public summary for the owner. Failures stay on the record.
value.notice_rule: Whoever notices a problem records it. A worker that notices one during any other verb, in any pack, returns a proposed record-finding verb with its evidence in proposed_verbs, and an authorized requester enqueues it; a person can claim record-finding directly. Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

flow.when: As soon as anyone notices a problem, even one that will be fixed a minute later.
When the problem needs to be seen again before a fix; security findings go to the security review pack instead.
After recording: fold duplicates together by fingerprint, then set kind, severity and sensitivity. Rerun it when a reproduction, fix, verification or guard points at the finding.
For a triaged finding; an annoyance or other matter of taste gets two or three options for a person.
For the chosen option: a test fails first, then passes.
By a different worker than the fixer, where the problem was seen.
When the fix has no guard yet, or its guard has not been shown to fail without the fix.
When the close gate can pass; deterministic.
Only when the disclosure rules allow it; the owner decides whether and where it appears.
Periodically, across closed findings, for causes that keep coming back.

rules: Record first. Recording never waits for a fix, a reproduction or a decision.
Failures stay on the record. Nothing is deleted or rewritten to hide a mistake; later steps write new versions or new nouns.
An annoyance is a real finding. When its fix is a matter of taste, a person chooses, never an agent.
The worker who made a fix does not verify it.
A guard counts only after it is shown to fail without the fix and pass with it.
Never publish details of an unfixed security finding.

shape.note: The flow follows the reproduce-then-repair breakdown pattern, with a person's checkpoint for taste calls.

related_packs.use: add-regression-guard proves a guard with its trust rule, and review-checks confirms the verdict.
propose-fix writes a palette brief for an annoyance or other taste call, and the person's choice decides the fix.
A security finding is scoped, reproduced in a local sandbox and fixed through it, and stays private until fixed everywhere.
A documentation finding can be audited and rewritten through it.
A fix too large for one verb becomes a proposed breakdown.

A fix that would build something new, such as a shared tool or check, first surveys what already exists and lays out the alternatives; a repair that restores something to its own tested contract does not need to.

provenance_notes.quote: everytime we notice some error, issue, design flaw, design annnoyance, etc we should create nouns and verbs for them

Entries marked not public were left out. nouns.title: How every noticed problem becomes nouns and verbs
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with its guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: record-finding writes the finding the moment the problem is noticed.
reproduce shows it happening again, in the smallest way that still fails.
triage folds duplicates together by fingerprint and sets kind, severity and sensitivity.
propose-fix names the cause and one to three options, each with the guard that would show it works.
fix makes the chosen option with a test that fails first.
verify-fix, by a different worker, reruns the reproduction on the unfixed and fixed versions.
add-regression-guard shows a guard failing without the fix and passing with it.
close applies the gate and writes the closing version of the finding.
publish-finding prepares a public summary when the disclosure rules allow it.
review-patterns looks across findings for causes that keep coming back.
rules: Record every noticed error, issue, design flaw or annoyance, even one fixed a minute later. Recording never waits.
Failures stay on the record. Never delete or rewrite a finding to hide a mistake; Tessera keeps every version.
One finding per problem: triage folds duplicates into the oldest finding with the same fingerprint, which keeps all their evidence.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs. They never enqueue; an authorized requester decides which proposals run.
The fixer never verifies their own fix.
A guard is trusted only after it fails without the fix and passes with it, twice, by the checks of checks trust rule.
A matter of taste is decided by a person through a taste palette; silence is never a choice.
Merged is not deployed: a fix merged but not running where the problem was seen leaves the finding fixed_not_deployed.
When a fix needs an authority nobody has given, such as a new spending allowance or a changed limit, record blocked with one question and never work around it.

statuses.open: Recorded; nobody is making a fix yet.
statuses.in_progress: A fix is being proposed or made.
statuses.fixed: A fix is in place where the problem lives.
statuses.fixed_not_deployed: The fix is merged but not running where the problem was seen.
statuses.verified: A different worker confirmed the fix where the problem was seen.
statuses.closed: The close gate passed: verified independently, with a guard shown to fail without the fix or a written waiver.
statuses.duplicate: Folded into an older finding with the same fingerprint, which keeps its evidence.
statuses.wont_fix: A person decided not to fix it, with a reason; it stays on the record.

resolved: A verification by a different worker than the fixer says fix_verified where the problem was seen.
A guard is shown to fail without the fix and pass with it, or a waiver gives the written reason no guard can run.
The closing version passes every record check.
duplicate: The pinned canonical finding lists this finding among its duplicates.
wont_fix: A person's recorded decision is pinned; an agent alone never decides not to fix.

follow_ups: New problems found while fixing or verifying become proposed record-finding verbs, never silent extra changes.
A fixed finding without a trusted guard gets a proposed add-regression-guard verb.
A cause seen in several places gets a proposed review-patterns run.

An option that would build something new, rather than repair something to its own tested contract, gets the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing and research-alternatives verbs proposed first.

nouns.title: The four kinds of finding, how to tell them apart and the fingerprint rule
nouns.category_reason: A reusable classification guide that every recording and triage verb applies.

error.means: Something gives a wrong result, crashes, leaks or accepts what it should refuse.
error.evidence: A minimal reproduction, a log excerpt or a measurement.
error.usual_fix: A code or configuration change with a test that fails without it.

issue.means: Something is missing, stale, misconfigured or waiting on a person, or a step in a process went wrong, without wrong behavior in the code itself.
issue.evidence: A link, receipt, status code or timestamp; for a process issue, the direction that applied and the action that broke it, with times.
issue.usual_fix: Content, configuration, a person's action or a change to the process.
issue.usual_guard: A link or contract check, or a process rule.

design_flaw.means: It works as built, but the design fails a person or another part: a layout that breaks at one width, text too faint to read, a generator that writes its clone folder's name into shared files.
design_flaw.evidence: Screenshots at named widths and themes for anything visual; otherwise the input that shows the flaw.
design_flaw.usual_guard: A page check at the named widths and themes, or a test of the property.

annoyance.means: Nothing is broken, but it bothers a person who uses or owns it: vague wording, an old name that keeps coming back, a format they did not want. An annoyance is a real finding.
annoyance.evidence: The person's words, verbatim, with who said them, when, and where the annoying thing appears.
annoyance.usual_fix: Often a matter of taste: two or three options, and the person chooses through the taste palettes pack.
annoyance.usual_guard: A check that the old wording or format does not return, once the person has chosen.

telling_them_apart: Wrong behavior against a spec, a test or a promise: error.
Behavior as built, but the design fails someone or something: design_flaw.
Nothing wrong, but a person is bothered: annoyance.
Missing, stale, misconfigured, blocked or a mistake in a process: issue.
When two fit, pick the one whose fix you expect and say why; triage can change it.
value.security: Any kind can also be a security finding: set sensitivity to security when it could expose data, grant access or spend beyond a grant. It stays private and goes through the security review pack until its fix is in effect everywhere it was seen.

fingerprint_rule.component: The smallest named part where it was seen, in lowercase words joined by hyphens, without paths, line numbers, versions or dates.
fingerprint_rule.symptom: Two to six lowercase words joined by hyphens for what goes wrong, without names, ids or numbers that change.
fingerprint_rule.duplicates: Equal fingerprints are duplicates. The same kind and component with a different symptom is a judgment call, so triage says why it folded them together or kept them apart.

nouns.title: Severity guide: P0 to P3
nouns.category_reason: A scoring rubric that every finding is rated against.

P0.means: Harm is happening now: credentials or personal data exposed, money spent without authority, or a surface down for everyone.
P0.respond: Contain it first and stop other work.

P1.means: Wrong or missing results that people would rely on, or a path by which someone without the grant can read, write or spend.
P1.respond: Fix before building on the affected work.

P2.means: A real problem with a narrow trigger or a known workaround, a scope mistake only an already authorized caller can trigger, a process mistake that was caught and undone, or an annoyance the owner made a rule about.

P3.means: Cosmetic, stale or minor, with no wrong results: a layout problem at one width, a count out of date, a portability trap with a workaround.
P3.respond: Fix when nearby, or batch similar ones.

rules: Rate the impact on people and work, not the effort to fix.
The noticer sets a provisional level; triage confirms or changes it with a reason.
Never lower a level to make a finding look smaller. A tested workaround can lower it by one level, and the workaround is named.
A cause that keeps coming back can be raised by one level in a pattern review.
value.worked_examples_note: The worked examples are listed at the levels their noticers gave them.

relations: security severities map onto these levels

nouns.title: Evidence checklist for each kind of finding
nouns.category_reason: Acceptance criteria that recording, reproduction and verification are checked against.

every_finding: What was seen, in one sentence; where; who noticed it; when, as a UTC date and time.
At least one piece of evidence a different worker could use to see the same problem.
Files, logs and screenshots stored by SHA-256, with credentials, personal data and private paths removed.
Anything not captured is marked unknown rather than guessed.

error: A minimal reproduction: the exact version or commit, the smallest input or command, and the expected and actual results.
Or a log excerpt with secrets removed, or a measurement with its method and sample size.
design_flaw: For anything visual: screenshots at named widths, by default 320, 768 and 1440 pixels, in every theme the surface offers, such as light and dark, with the page address and version.
For a flaw that is not visual: the input that shows it, such as the folder name or setting that triggers it.
annoyance: The person's words, verbatim, with who said them and when.
Where the annoying thing appears; two or three places are enough.
issue: The link, receipt, run id, status code or timestamp that shows it.
For a process issue: the direction that applied, where it was written, and the action that broke it, with times.

never: A credential value; say where it was, never what it was.
A screenshot or log that shows personal data or someone else's private information.
A claim of reproduction without a recorded run.

nouns.title: Disclosure rules for findings
nouns.category_reason: Guardrails that decide which findings may ever be described in public.

rules: Never publish details of an unfixed security finding. A security finding stays private until its fix is in effect everywhere the problem was seen; fixed_not_deployed is not enough.
Fixed findings, and findings with nothing sensitive in them, may be published once their owner agrees.
A finding marked public false stays private, even after it is fixed.
Never publish credentials, personal data, private names, private paths or private notes. Say where a secret was, never its value.
A public summary is a separate noun written for readers outside the team; the finding itself stays in the team's scope.
Publishing is the owner's act on a surface of their choice. No verb in this pack publishes anything.
Failures stay on the record in public too: a summary says plainly what went wrong, including mistakes in process.

deterministic_gate.check: The finding's public field is true.
A finding with sensitivity security has status fixed, verified or closed.
Sensitivity is none or security; credential, personal data and private context findings are never published.
The record checks' secret pattern finds nothing in the summary.
Every link is a public https address or a public pull request or commit reference.

relations: security findings keep its private, local-only handling

nouns.title: Record checks for findings, with real and made-up golden findings
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with golden fixtures and recorded expected results that the validator recomputes.

value.purpose: Checks every version of a finding must pass before triage, close or publish-finding accept it. The eight real public findings in this pack pass all of them; each made-up known-bad finding fails exactly the one check named in fails. The validator recomputes every verdict.

deterministic_checks.why: Every finding is one of the four kinds, so triage and the evidence checklist apply.
Severity uses the guide's four levels.
Status uses the method's eight meanings.
The disclosure rules depend on sensitivity.
A finding shows what was seen.
Who noticed it is part of the record.
When it was noticed is part of the record.
Triage folds duplicates together by fingerprint.
An error comes with a reproduction, a log excerpt or a measurement.
A design flaw comes with screenshots, or for anything not visual the input that shows it.
An annoyance is recorded in the person's own words.
A finding marked fixed says what the fix is.
A fix is verified by a different worker than the one who made it.
A closed finding has a guard shown to fail without the fix, or a waiver.
A waiver says why no guard can run.
A duplicate points at the finding that keeps its evidence.
Only a person's recorded decision closes a finding as won't fix.
Credential, personal data and private context findings are never published.
Never publish details of an unfixed security finding; fixed_not_deployed is not enough.
Say where a secret is, never its value.

cause_shared is true when the same cause lives in several copies; the shared fix is then one of the options.

nouns.title: Template: a regression guard: the test or check, its runs with and without the fix and a trust verdict by the checks of checks rule

A process rule is needs_judges until two judges or a person agree on it.
A deterministic check uses only the checks of checks rule types.

verbs.title: Record a noticed problem as a finding
verbs.summary: Write down an error, issue, design flaw or annoyance as soon as anyone notices it: what was seen, where, evidence, who noticed it and when, a provisional kind and severity, and a fingerprint for spotting duplicates.
verbs.outcome: A finding noun with status open, or no_change when this exact observation by this noticer is already recorded.

slots.name: evidence_records
slots.description: Pins of runs, check results or logs that already show the problem, if any.

slots.name: nearby_findings
slots.description: Pins of findings already recorded for the same part, to compare fingerprints. A match is noted for triage, not skipped.

finding_id.description: The id the requester assigned to the new finding.

observation.description: What was seen, in the noticer's own words.

where.description: Where it was seen: a file and line, a page address, a run id or a step in a process.

noticed_by.description: Who noticed it: a person, a worker or an automated check.

noticed_at.description: When it was noticed, as a UTC date and time.

steps: Record it now, even if it looks small or will be fixed in a minute; recording never waits for a fix.
Write what was seen, where, who noticed it and when. For an annoyance, quote the person's words exactly.
Attach the evidence the checklist names for its kind and mark anything missing as unknown instead of guessing.

Choose a provisional kind and severity from the guides and compute the fingerprint by the kind definitions' rule. Compare it with any pinned nearby findings and note a match instead of skipping the record.

Remove credentials, personal data and private paths; say where a secret is, never its value. Set sensitivity to security, and public to false, when the problem could expose data, grant access or spend beyond a grant.
Set status open. Never delete or rewrite an earlier finding; a correction is a later version or a new finding.

acceptance.check: The finding validates against template.finding's schema.
The finding passes every deterministic check in record-checks.
The fingerprint starts with the finding's kind.
The status is open.
A different worker could see the same problem from the evidence.

notes: Any worker on any verb, in any pack, can return this verb in its proposed_verbs when it notices a problem; an authorized requester enqueues it.

verbs.title: Reproduce the finding
verbs.summary: Show the problem happening again from the finding alone, at the exact version where it was seen and on the latest one, in the smallest way that still fails, so a fix can be checked against it.
verbs.outcome: A reproduction record: reproduced, not reproduced or inconclusive, with versions, steps and evidence by digest.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the finding.

slots.name: snapshot
slots.description: Pin of a snapshot of the code or page at the version where the problem was seen.

version.description: The exact commit, release or page address and date where the problem was seen.

steps: Verify the pins. If the finding's sensitivity is security, do not reproduce it here: end blocked, ask for the security review pack's scope check and propose its check-scope verb.
Reproduce at the exact version where it was seen, then on the latest version, and record each run.
Shrink the steps to the smallest input or command that still shows it. For a visual design flaw, capture screenshots at the named widths and themes; for an annoyance, show each place it appears.
Make only requests that change nothing, and only to public pages and files the finding names.
Store logs and screenshots by SHA-256 with secrets removed. If it does not reproduce, say so: not reproduced is a result, not a failure.

acceptance.check: The reproduction validates against template.reproduction's schema.
Every run names its exact version, or page address and date.
result is reproduced only when a recorded run shows the problem.
The steps are the smallest that still show the problem.

network: Requests that change nothing, only to public pages and files named in the finding, and package downloads for a sandbox build. Never to a system named in a security finding.
capabilities: write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Triage the finding
verbs.summary: Fold duplicates together by fingerprint, then set the finding's kind, severity and sensitivity from the guides and choose its route. Rerun it when a reproduction, fix, verification or guard points at the finding, to link them and move its status forward.
verbs.outcome: A new version of the finding with kind, severity, sensitivity, duplicates and route set, or marked as a duplicate of an older finding.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the current version of the finding to triage.

slots.name: other_findings
slots.description: Pins of findings that may be duplicates, such as those with the same component.

slots.name: runs
slots.description: Pins of reproductions and verifications that point at this finding.

slots.name: fixes
slots.description: Pins of fixes made for this finding.

slots.name: guards
slots.description: Pins of regression guards for this finding.

steps: Verify the pins. Compare fingerprints: an equal fingerprint is a duplicate; the same kind and component with a different symptom is a judgment call, so say why you folded it in or kept it apart.

If an older finding has the same fingerprint, mark this one as its duplicate and propose a triage of the older finding with this one's evidence. Otherwise list the duplicates here, copy their evidence references in and propose closing each one as a duplicate.
Set kind and severity from the guides with a reason for each. Keep the noticer's values when they fit, and never lower a severity to make a finding look smaller.

Set sensitivity and the route: a security finding stays private and goes to the security review pack, a documentation finding can go to the docs improvement pack, and an annoyance whose fix is a matter of taste is marked for a person's choice.

On a rerun, link the pinned runs, fixes and guards and move the status forward: in_progress, fixed, fixed_not_deployed when the fix is merged but not deployed where the problem was seen, or verified. Never set closed or wont_fix here.
Write one new version of the pinned finding with its current version as the compare-and-set expectation; a version conflict means re-read and stop.

acceptance.check: The new version validates against template.finding's schema.
The new version passes every deterministic check in record-checks.
Every finding listed as a duplicate, or named in duplicate_of, is among the pinned findings.
The status is not closed or wont_fix.
The write used the pinned version as its expected version.
The kind and severity reasons cite the guides.

notes: This verb updates the finding through compare-and-set. Each run writes one new version, and every earlier version stays readable, so failures stay on the record.

verbs.title: Propose a fix
verbs.summary: From the finding and its reproduction, propose the smallest fix that removes the cause, with the guard that would show it works. For an annoyance or another matter of taste, offer two or three options for a person to choose between.
verbs.outcome: A fix proposal with one to three options, the cause it addresses and each option's guard, plus a palette brief when a person's taste call is needed.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the triaged finding.

slots.name: reproduction
slots.description: Pin of its reproduction.

slots.name: snapshot
slots.description: Pin of a snapshot of the code or page.

slots.name: earlier_findings
slots.description: Pins of earlier findings for the same part, so the proposal does not repeat a fix that failed.

slots.name: survey
slots.description: Pin of a survey of what already exists for this fix, from the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing verb.

slots.name: alternatives
slots.description: Pin of the alternatives that pack's research-alternatives verb laid out for this fix, including reuse as is, adapt and do nothing.

steps: Verify the pins. Name the cause, not just the symptom, and read the pinned earlier findings so the proposal does not repeat a fix that already failed.
Prefer the smallest change that removes the cause where it lives. When the same cause lives in several copies, say so and include the shared fix as an option.

Mark each option repair or build. A repair restores something to its own tested contract. For a build, such as a new shared tool or check, base the option on the pinned survey and alternatives and prefer reusing or adapting what exists; without them, propose the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing and research-alternatives verbs first.
For each option, say what changes, what could break and which guard would fail without it and pass with it.

For an annoyance or any other matter of taste, offer two or three options with plain differences and no recommendation, and write a palette brief from the taste palettes template so a person chooses; never choose on their behalf.
When the fix is too large for one verb, propose a breakdown through the decomposition patterns pack instead of one large fix.
If the fix needs an authority nobody has given, such as a new spending allowance or a changed limit, end blocked with that one question.

acceptance.check: The proposal validates against template.fix-proposal's schema.
A taste call has two or three options and no recommended option.
Every option names the guard that would fail without it.
Every option marked build cites the pinned survey, or survey-existing is among the proposed verbs.
A palette brief is produced exactly when the proposal is a taste call, and it validates against the taste palettes brief template.
The options address the cause the reproduction shows.

verbs.title: Make the fix
verbs.summary: Make the chosen option in a local copy: first a test or check that fails for the finding's reason, then the smallest change that makes it pass, with the existing checks still passing, stored by digest.
verbs.outcome: A fix record with the patch digest, the changed files, the test that failed before and passed after and the suite result; landing it is the owner's separate act.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the finding.

slots.name: fix_proposal
slots.description: Pin of the fix proposal.

slots.name: reproduction
slots.description: Pin of the reproduction.

slots.name: choice
slots.description: Pin of the person's recorded choice when the proposal was a taste call.

slots.name: snapshot
slots.description: Pin of a snapshot of the code or page.

option.description: The option to make, A to C; for a taste call, the option the person chose.

steps: Verify the pins. For a taste call, make only the option the person chose; a choice of none ends no_change.
Write the test or check first and run it on the unfixed copy: it must fail for the finding's reason. If it cannot be made to fail, end unknown and say what is missing.
Make the smallest change that makes it pass, then run the existing checks. Never delete, skip or loosen another check to get a pass.
For a visual design flaw, capture screenshots after the change at the same widths and themes as the finding.
Store the patch by digest in the requester's scope. Do not push, merge or open a pull request; landing the fix is the owner's separate act.

acceptance.check: The fix validates against template.fix's schema.
The added test failed on the unfixed copy and passed after the change, in recorded runs.
suite_passed is true from an actual run.
No existing test or check was deleted, skipped or loosened.
The change is the smallest that removes the cause.

network: Package installs inside the sandbox to run the existing checks. No requests to any deployed system.
capabilities: write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Verify the fix independently
verbs.summary: A different worker than the one who made the fix reruns the reproduction on the unfixed and the fixed versions, where the problem was seen when possible, and checks that the problem is gone without new ones.
verbs.outcome: A verification: fix_verified, fix_failed or inconclusive, with both runs and where they ran.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the finding.

slots.name: fix
slots.description: Pin of the fix.

slots.name: reproduction
slots.description: Pin of the reproduction.

where_checked.description: Where this verification runs. Use where the problem was seen when you can.

steps: Confirm you wrote neither the fix nor its proposal; otherwise end blocked.
Rerun the reproduction on the unfixed and the fixed versions: the first must still show the problem and the second must not.
Say where you checked. A fix checked only on a local copy or a merged branch is not verified for a problem seen on a deployed surface.
For a visual design flaw, compare screenshots at the finding's widths and themes; for an annoyance, check every place the finding names.
Record any new problem the fix caused as a proposed record-finding verb; never fix it inside this verb.

acceptance.check: The verification validates against template.verification's schema.
The verifying key differs from the keys that wrote the fix and its proposal.
Recorded runs exist for the unfixed and the fixed versions.
fix_verified only when the unfixed run shows the problem and the fixed run does not.

network: Requests that change nothing, only to public pages and files named in the finding, and package downloads for a sandbox build. Never to a system named in a security finding.
capabilities: write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Add a regression guard
verbs.summary: Write or adopt a test or check that would catch the problem coming back, and prove it with the checks of checks trust rule: it passes on the fixed version and fails on the unfixed one, twice each.
verbs.outcome: A regression guard record with its runs and a trusted, revise, reject or needs_judges verdict.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the finding.

slots.name: fix
slots.description: Pin of the fix.

slots.name: verification
slots.description: Pin of the verification.

guard_kind.description: The kind of guard: an automated test, a deterministic check, a page check or a process rule.

steps: Verify the pins. Prefer adopting a test the fix already added; otherwise write the smallest test or check that encodes the reproduction.
Run the guard on the fixed version and on the unfixed version, twice each. It is trusted only when it passes on the fixed version and fails on the unfixed one for the finding's reason, both times.
A guard that passes on the unfixed version is too weak: record revise and say what it misses. A guard that fails on the fixed version is wrong: record reject.
A deterministic check uses only the checks of checks rule types; a page check names its widths and themes; a process rule is a judgment check, needs_judges until two judges or a person agree.
Propose the checks of checks review-checks verb, so a different worker confirms the verdict.

acceptance.check: The guard validates against template.regression-guard's schema.
trusted only when both fixed runs passed and both unfixed runs failed; otherwise the verdict the trust rule gives.
The second pass gave the same results as the first.
The unfixed runs failed for the finding's reason, not an unrelated error.

network: Package installs inside the sandbox to run the existing checks. No requests to any deployed system.
capabilities: write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Close the finding
verbs.summary: Apply the close gate and, when it passes, write the finding's closing version: resolved with an independent verification and a guard shown to fail without the fix or a written waiver, a duplicate of a named finding, or won't fix by a person's decision.
verbs.outcome: A new version of the finding with status closed, duplicate or wont_fix and the gate results, or no_change listing the gate checks that failed.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the current version of the finding.

slots.name: verification
slots.description: Pin of the independent verification, for resolved.

slots.name: guard
slots.description: Pin of the regression guard, for resolved.

slots.name: canonical
slots.description: Pin of the older finding this one duplicates, for duplicate.

slots.name: decision
slots.description: Pin of a person's recorded decision not to fix, such as a taste palette choice of none, for wont_fix.

waiver.description: For resolved without a trusted guard: the written reason no guard can run. Leave null otherwise.

steps: Verify the pins, then apply the gate for the reason given. Every gate check must pass; a failed check ends no_change with the checks that failed and the verbs that would satisfy them.

Resolved: a verification by a different worker than the fixer says fix_verified where the problem was seen, and a guard is trusted or a waiver gives its reason. A fix merged but not deployed where the problem was seen stays fixed_not_deployed.
Duplicate: the pinned canonical finding lists this finding among its duplicates.
Won't fix: a person's recorded decision is pinned; an agent alone never closes a finding as won't fix.
Write the closing version with its current version as the compare-and-set expectation, with links to the fix, the verification and the guard. Never remove earlier evidence or history.

acceptance.check: The closing version validates against template.finding's schema.
The closing version passes every deterministic check in record-checks.
Every gate check for the given reason is recorded with its result in output.checks.
For wont_fix, the pinned decision was written by a person's key.
The write used the pinned version as its expected version.

notes: Deterministic: the gate reads pinned nouns only and calls no model. Like triage, it updates the finding through compare-and-set and keeps every earlier version.

verbs.title: Prepare a finding for publication
verbs.summary: When the disclosure rules allow it, write a short public summary of a finding: what went wrong, what changed and how a guard keeps it from coming back, with public links only. The owner decides whether and where it appears; this verb never publishes anything.
verbs.outcome: A public summary that passed every disclosure check, waiting for the owner, or no_change naming the rule that does not allow it yet.

slots.name: finding
slots.description: Pin of the finding.

slots.name: fix
slots.description: Pin of the fix.

slots.name: verification
slots.description: Pin of the verification.

slots.name: guard
slots.description: Pin of the regression guard.

steps: Verify the pins and apply the disclosure gate first. An unfixed security finding, a finding marked public false, or one holding credentials or personal data ends no_change, and nothing about it is drafted.
Write for a reader outside the team: what was seen, its kind and severity, what changed, how a guard keeps it from coming back, and links only to public pull requests, commits and pages.
Say plainly what went wrong, including mistakes in process; failures stay on the record.
Remove private names, private paths, keys, personal data and anything else the rules list, and record each redaction.
Mark the summary as the owner's decision with approved false. Releasing it is the owner's separate act, on a surface of their choice.

acceptance.check: The summary validates against template.public-summary's schema.
Every disclosure gate check passed for this finding.
The record checks' secret pattern finds nothing in the summary.
release_decision is owner and approved is false.
Every statement matches the finding and its linked nouns.

verbs.title: Review patterns across findings
verbs.summary: Periodically look across closed findings, and open ones with the same cause, for causes that keep coming back, and propose upstream fixes, such as one shared repair for a bug copied into many repositories.
verbs.outcome: A pattern review listing repeated causes with their findings, counts, places and the upstream fix each needs, or no_change when no cause repeats.

slots.name: findings
slots.description: Pins of the findings to review: closed ones, and open ones that may share a cause.

slots.name: earlier_reviews
slots.description: Pins of earlier pattern reviews, to see whether an upstream fix stopped its cause.

window_from.description: First date of the review window.

window_to.description: Last date of the review window.

min_findings.description: Fewest findings that make a pattern, unless one finding is seen in several places.

steps: Verify the pins. Group findings by cause, not by wording: the same component in the fingerprint, the same guard, the same copied file or the same missed step.
A pattern needs at least min_findings findings, or one finding seen in several places, such as a script copied into every repository.

For each pattern, say where one upstream fix would cover every instance, such as a shared kit, template, checklist or generator, and propose a record-finding verb for the shared cause, the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing verb for what already exists, and a propose-fix verb. Do not make the fix here.
Read the earlier reviews: a cause that came back after its upstream fix is itself a new finding, so propose recording it.

acceptance.check: The review validates against template.pattern-review's schema.
Every count equals the number of findings listed in its pattern.
Every finding named in a pattern is among the pinned findings.
Each upstream fix addresses the shared cause, not one instance.

notes: Periodic: run it weekly or after every ten closed findings, whichever comes first. This pack activates no schedule; a recurring run needs Tessera's flag-gated schedule support and an authorized requester.
